annotation.title_clean: A Review of - Humans and Robots: Ethics, Agency, and Anthropomorphism by Sven Nyholm
annotation.title_en: A Review of - Humans and Robots: Ethics, Agency, and Anthropomorphism by Sven Nyholm
annotation.venue: Journal of Ethics and Emerging Technologies
annotation.summary_en: Book review of Sven Nyholm's "Humans and Robots," which treats the ethics of human-robot interaction through robot agency, anthropomorphism and case studies (self-driving cars, autonomous weapons, sex robots). The reviewer praises the framework but criticises unclear human/robot demarcation and the agency attribution versus recognition distinction.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robot agency is a distinct kind of agency, held to standards different from human agency.
Humans are psychologically and institutionally poorly prepared for robots, tending to anthropomorphize them.
Legal notions of agency do not map onto robotic agency, complicating responsibility.
Humanoid robots may warrant respectful treatment, so 'recognition' fits better than 'attribution'.
The book is useful to beginners, experts and legal professionals.
